CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
1. Region means Pringsewu Regency. 2. Regional Government means the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent means the Regent of Pringsewu. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regional Secretary means the Regional Secretary of Pringsewu Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a regional apparatus in Pringsewu Regency. 7. Woman means an adult human of female gender. 8. Child means a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb. 9. Child victim of violence means a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policy, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and society. 10. Victim means a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women means any act of violence against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 13. Violence against children means any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means actions by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal assistance means legal services provided by legal companions and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of another person. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Companion means a person or institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and child victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Accompaniment means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER XI
CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 12
Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f is caused by:
a. threat of violence includes: any act unlawfully in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, either with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is forced to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 5
The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes prevention efforts, services, and empowerment for victims of violence in the region.

CHAPTER VI
DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 23
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER X
REPORTING
Article 21
(1) PPT reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
(2) The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 12
Letter a Sufficiently clear.
Letter b What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain explanations, statements, ideas, and signs that contain value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts, or their explanations, which can be seen, heard, and read, presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology, electronically or non-electronically, related to acts of violence.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "the right to continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" includes: the right to have one’s rights advocated for and access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.
Letter e What is meant by "the right to confidential handling" is the right of victims to have their identity kept confidential at all stages of handling by officers.
Letter f What is meant by "the right to psychological and legal assistance" is a right that includes assistance by: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members.
Letter g Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XIV
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 25
(1) Officials appointed to organize integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the applicable Laws and Regulations;
(2) PPT managers who in carrying out the duties of protection, services and recovery for victims of violence, violate the principles of organizing protection, services and recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of PPT and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 20
(1) The forms of protection provided to Victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of protection:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

CHAPTER XIII
FUNDING
Article 24 (1) Regional governments are obligated to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in carrying out the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) The budget allocation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be adjusted to the regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 11
Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE
Article 1
Sufficiently clear.
Article 2
What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal rights and human dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.
What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.
What is meant by "protection of the human rights of women and children" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that in all actions concerning the victim carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 1
Sufficiently clear.
Article 2
What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal rights and human dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.
What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.
What is meant by "protection of the human rights of women and children" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 23
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Victim means a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 11. Violence means any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim. 12. Violence against women means any act of violence against women that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 13. Violence against children means any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom. 14. Physical violence means any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and or causes death. 15. Sexual violence means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 16. Economic violence means any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper living, care or maintenance. 17. Neglect means the act of neglecting women and or children within the household scope which according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide living, care or maintenance to that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by limiting and or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 18. Psychological violence means any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, sense of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Protection of women means all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur or has occurred. 20. Law enforcement means actions by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal assistance means legal services provided by legal companions and advocates to conduct the process of accompanying witnesses and or victims of violence against women and children. 22. Protection of children means all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Implementation of protection means a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center. 24. Prevention means direct efforts made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 25. Complaint means notification either in writing or orally by an interested party to an authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers loss due to the actions of another person. 26. Service means immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Companion means a person or institution that has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy, advocacy for the empowerment and self-recovery of victims of violence. 28. Integrated Service means a series of activities to provide protection for women and child victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unit of implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence. 29. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Accompaniment means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER X
REPORTING
Article 21
(1) PPT reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
(2) The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XI
CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regent implements control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
(2) Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 23
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER III
SCOPE
Article 5
The scope of protection for women and children victims of violence includes prevention efforts, services, and empowerment for victims of violence in the region.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 2

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.
What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.
What is meant by "protection of the human rights of women and children" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 23
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

Article 21
(1) PPT reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
(2) The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XIII

Article 24 (1) Regional governments are obligated to allocate budget to the integrated service center (PPT) in carrying out the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.

Article 2 The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VI
DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

a. threat of violence includes: any act unlawfully in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, either with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is forced to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

Article 1
Sufficiently clear.
Article 2
What is meant by "respect and recognition of equal rights and human dignity" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and guarantee the fulfillment of victims' rights in order to uphold human dignity.
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is not making distinctions on any grounds or in any manner, whether concerning religion and beliefs, ethnicity, race, gender, skin color, language, and politics.
What is meant by "gender equality and justice" is a process to be fair to both men and women in obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities as well as equality in enjoying the results of development.
What is meant by "protection of the human rights of women and children" is providing human rights in the form of security to women carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that in all actions concerning the victim carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on the principles of respect for and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the human rights of Women and Children and the best interests of victims.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

(2) The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20
(1) The forms of protection provided to Victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of protection:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.

CHAPTER VI
DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that provides integrated services for victims of violence in the region. 30. Victim Recovery means all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually. 31. Accompaniment means all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced. 32.

CHAPTER X
REPORTING
Article 21
(1) PPT reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
(2) The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports activities on prevention, handling and protection of women and children victims of violence to the Regent.
(3) The Regent reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20
(1) The forms of protection provided to Victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of protection:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER XII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 23
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community;
b. establishing women and child protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights;
d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent agency if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, community social institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

CHAPTER VI
DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.

c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

CHAPTER IX
IMPLEMENTATION, FORMS OF PROTECTION AND SERVICES
Article 19
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the PPT framework.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, the PPT may, in its implementation, establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, customs, and the rights and obligations of parents/guardians, husbands and/or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented according to Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), which are further regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 20

a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

REGARDING

I. GENERAL
One of the materials of the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia is the guarantee of human rights and constitutional rights of citizens. The Amendment can be interpreted as a manifestation of awareness about the importance of protecting human rights and constitutional rights of citizens, which grew and became the spirit of reform. Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination.
Every citizen has human rights that must be guaranteed by the state to obtain a sense of security, be protected and be free from all forms of violence. Women and children are vulnerable groups, therefore they need to receive protection from the state that can provide prevention and protection for victims of violence.
Regional governments together with the community are obligated to organize prevention, protection and recovery efforts for children and women victims of violence for the sake of honor and protection of human dignity and worth.
Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in Pringsewu Regency.

What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that in all actions concerning the victim carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Article 20
(1) The forms of protection provided to Victims, witnesses and reporters organized by PPT are in the form of protection:
a. medical;
b. legal;
c. medicolegal (Forensic Medicine);
d. psychological; or
e. economic.
(2) The form of medical protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is in the form of treatment and recovery from physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics.
(3) The form of legal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is in the form of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is in the form of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of psychological protection for Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is in the form of assistance in order to restore traumatic conditions including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and provide psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.
(6) The form of economic protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1), is in the form of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.

SCOPE

DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government has the duty to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, by:
a. collecting data and information about Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
c. providing education about anti-violence values against children and women; and
d. conducting monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of protection for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) The Regional Government has the obligation to undertake prevention efforts, handling and recovery of victims of violence against Women and Children, providing and organizing services for victims in the form of:
a. providing and facilitating the establishment of integrated services for victims by involving institutions and community elements;
b. encouraging public awareness about the importance of protection for victims; and
c. conducting community empowerment for the prevention of acts of violence.
